MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  January 23, 2018

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Sachs at 5:00 p.m., on January 23, 2018, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on January 18, 2018, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman
P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Bucknum
  Council Member Goodell
  Council Member Kelley
  Mayor Pro Tem Raths
  Mayor Sachs

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Legal Counsel-Existing Litigation: Paragraph (1) of subdivision (d)
  of Section 54956.9; Name of case: Webster et al vs. City of Mission Viejo.

CS2. Conference with Legal Counsel -- Anticipated Litigation. Significant exposure to
  litigation pursuant to subdivision (b) of Section 54956.9: one case. Initiation of
  litigation pursuant to paragraph (4) of subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9: one case.

City Council Minutes  1  January 23, 2018
 RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:01 p.m., Mayor Sachs recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:03 p.m. with all five Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the City Council considered two matters involving
litigation in Closed Session. The Council received updates and gave direction to staff but no
reportable action occurred.

INVOCATION: Mayor Pro Tem Raths

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Goodell

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Recognize the 2017 Employees of the Year

  Mayor Sachs and staff presented plaques to (1) Community Services Supervisor, Carren
  Chaney, City of Mission Viejo Employee of the Year; (2) Deputy, Travis Krudwig, Orange
  County Sheriff’s Department Employee of the Year; and (3) Firefighter, Chris Linton,
  Orange County Fire Authority Employee of the Year.

P2.  Recognize Coach Rose as a Home Town Hero

  Mayor Sachs and Council Member Bucknum presented the proclamation to Bill Rose,
  retiring Head Coach of the Nadadores Swim Club.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Jennifer Golden, M.V.: announced that she is representing Mary Navarro who is running for
District 5 Trustee of the Orange County Board of Education, and she discussed Ms. Navarro’s
background and skills.

Alison Mitchell, M.V.: stated that she is a big proponent of public education and is very excited
about Mary Navarro's qualifications for Orange County Board of Education, District 5. She said
that one of Mary’s core principals is that education is a right for all ages and should be affordable
and accessible.

Mary Navarro, Dana Point: announced that she is proud to stand before the City Council and share
her passion and experience in education. She asked for the Council’s support of her for District 5
Representative on the Orange County Board of Education and she invited residents to visit her
website at votemarynavarro.com.

Michael Rotcher, M.V.: thanked the City Council and staff for their prompt response to his email
about the Public Utility Commission’s (PUC) resolution on Community Choice Energy (CCE).
City Council Minutes  2  January 23, 2018
 Mr. Rotcher noted that the PUC has moved consideration of the matter to February so people have
time to more fully understand the proposal. He also announced that on April 11, 2018, OC Clean
Power is hosting a seminar on Community Choice Energy and invitations will go out soon.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Item 13 was removed from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration.

Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council meeting of January 9, 2018, as
  presented.

2.  Check Register Dated December 15, 2017 in the Amount of $2,392,872.81

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

3.  Check Register Dated December 22, 2017 in the Amount of $2,983,515.06

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Check Register Dated January 5, 2018 in the Amount of $871,315.85

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for November 2017

  Received and filed.

6.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing  Authority  (MVCDFA)
  Treasurer’s Monthly Report for November 2017

  Received and filed.

7.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for
  November 2017

  Received and filed.
City Council Minutes  3  January 23, 2018
 8.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly
  Report for November 2017

  Received and filed.

9.  Advocacy and Government Relations Services on behalf of Successor Agency of the
  Community Development Agency of the City of Mission Viejo

  Approved the Third Amendment to the Professional Services Agreement with Joe A.
  Gonsalves & Son for advocacy services for a total not to exceed the amount of $82,500.

10.  Review and Approval of Recognized Obligation Payment Schedule for the 18-19 A-B
  Annual Fiscal Period of July 1, 2018 to June 30, 2019

  (1) Adopted Successor Agency Resolution No. 18-01 Approving the Recognized
  Obligation Payment Schedule for the 18-19 A-B for the Annual Fiscal Period of July 1,
  2018, to June 30, 2019, Subject to Submittal to and Review by the Oversight and by the
  Department of Finance under the Division 24, Part 1.85 of the California Health and Safety
  Code, and Authorizing the Posting and Transmittal Thereof; and (2) further, the
  Administrative Services Director, in consultation with legal counsel, shall be authorized to
  request and complete meet and confer session(s), if any, with the Department of Finance
  and authorized to make augmentations, modifications, additions or revisions as may be
  necessary or directed by the Department of Finance.

11.  Claim Against the City - Glauber

  Rejected claim.

12.  Agreement for Consultant Services for Property Tax Consulting

  Approved Successor Agency Agreement for Consultant Services with HdL Coren & Cone
  for Property Tax Consulting Services in an amount not exceed $16,500 per fiscal year for
  the period of July 1, 2018, through June 30, 2022.

14.  Delegation of Authority to Request Disbursements from the Other Post Employment
  Prefunding Plan

  Adopted Resolution 18-05 Approving the Delegation of Authority to Request
  Disbursements from Other Post Employment Prefunding Plan.

15.  Trabuco Road and Marguerite Parkway Pavement Rehabilitation (CIP 18837)

  (1) Adopted Resolution 18-06 Amending the Fiscal Year 2017-2018 Budget for CIP
  18837; and (2) award the construction contract for the subject project to All American
  Asphalt in the amount of $2,257,257.00.

16.  Contract Amendment with Griffin Structures Inc. for Supplemental Staffing
City Council Minutes  4  January 23, 2018
   Approved Frist Amendment in the amount of $29,500 for supplemental staffing with Griffin
  Structures Inc.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

13.  Marguerite Parkway Corridor Traffic Signal Synchronization (CIP 17230)

  Council Member Kelley announced that she pulled this item from the Consent Calendar to
  highlight that residents will be seeing some traffic signal synchronization improvements to
  all 30 signals along the Marguerite Parkway corridor from Auto Mall to El Toro Road. In
  addition, there will be associated traffic signal infrastructure improvements along Olympiad
  Road from Marguerite Parkway to San Marcos.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to approve
  the bid plans and specifications, subject to minor revisions required by the City Engineer,
  and authorize staff to advertise for construction bids for the subject project.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

PUBLIC HEARINGS

17.  California Voting Rights Act Mapping Opportunities and Continued Request for
  Public Input

  City Attorney Bill Curley presented the staff report.

  Mayor Sachs opened the public hearing at 7:24 p.m.

  Gail Reavis, M.V.: read the definition of gerrymandering and said it describes Map Z. She
  commented on the other resident-submitted maps and a newspaper article about districts
  being ruled unconstitutional. Mrs. Reavis expressed her opposition to Map Z and to district
  elections as a whole.

  Larry Gilbert, M.V.: said that gerrymandering is when district lines are drawn to
  specifically favor one candidate, or a group of candidates, at the expense of the opposition
  or of the democratic process. Mr. Gilbert stated that the selection of Map Z would provide
  a huge advantage to the current City Council Members.

  Steve Serra, M.V.: referenced Professor Francisco Bethencourt’s book, Racism from the
  Crusades to the Twentieth Century in which he defines racism as "Prejudice concerning
  ethnic descent coupled with discriminatory action.” Mr. Serra noted that racist Latino
  voting is supposedly needed to cure racist voting and he asked the City Council to say no
  to districts.
City Council Minutes  5  January 23, 2018
   Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: said that she hopes the Council has done their due diligence and
  reviewed all materials available to evaluate how other cities have handled the districting
  process in their jurisdictions. She stated that the City Attorney should have directed the
  demographer to create more than one map and the Council has made no attempt to adjust
  the boundaries of Map Z. Ms. Schlicht said there is a strong appearance that the City has
  crafted a way to confuse or disparage public participation in the districting process.

  Gail Reavis, M.V.: completed her comments on the district maps and stated that the
  residents she has spoken to wish to continue voting in at-large elections.

  Mayor Sachs closed the public hearing at 7:36 p.m.

OLD BUSINESS

18.  Floor and Décor Confirming Resolution

  Director of Community Development Elaine Lister presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to
  adopt Resolution 18-07 Denying the Appeal Petition and Approving Minor Modification
  MM2017-421, Being a Petition Submitted By Centerpoint Integrated Solutions, to Permit
  Site and Building Modifications to Accommodate a New Floor & Décor Retail Business
  at 25872 Muirlands Boulevard, in the CC (Commercial Community) Zone.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

NEW BUSINESS

20.  Draft Request for Qualifications ("RFQ") and Proposals ("RFP") for affordable
  housing development prepared on behalf of the Mission Viejo Housing Authority of
  the City of Mission Viejo for an approximate 8.5 acre sub parcel zoned RPD-30A that
  is unimproved real property commonly referred to as "Site C" located on City-owned
  land directly adjacent to and southeasterly of the City’s Animal Service Center off
  Center Drive, and easterly of Saddleback College

  City Attorney Bill Curley presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Goodell, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Raths, to
  authorize the distribution of the RFQ/RFP to qualified developers of affordable housing.
  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
City Council Minutes  6  January 23, 2018
 OLD BUSINESS (Continued)

19.  Review of Insurance Coverage Options

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report and noted that
  staff is seeking the Council's direction as to whether the City should remain with the
  California Joint Powers Insurance Authority (CJPIA) or request formal proposals from the
  other insurance pools that are outlined in the agenda report.

  John Paulson, Bickmore: provided a brief overview of the analysis his firm performed and a
  summary of the conclusion.

  Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: presented written questions about claim settlements and rate increases
  and asked if the City leaves the JPIA, will that compromise or enhance the stability of the
  JPIA?

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to (1)
  continue to Phase II and seek formal cost proposals from the other agencies; and (2) adopt
  Resolution 18-08 Amending the Budget for Fiscal Year 2017-18 to Fund Risk Management
  Consulting Services.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

21.  Orange County Local Agency Formation Commission (LAFCO) Report

  Council Member Bucknum presented the report.

22.  Orange County Veteran’s Advisory Council

  Mayor Pro Tem Raths presented the report.

STAFF REPORTS

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

23.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities
  calendars as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk
  for the public record.

City Council Minutes  7  January 23, 2018
 Council Member Bucknum

Referencing agenda item 17, Council Member Bucknum stated that the first district map, Map Z,
was a starting point. It wasn't created by the City Council but was an example of what a map could
look like. She said it was never her intention to have Z be the final map, but rather to start a
conversation which is what happened. Council Member Bucknum said she wants the public to
understand that the Council is trying to look at this legal situation, as fiduciaries of the City, and
find the best way to protect the City. She said she’s heard from residents loud and clear that they
do not want districts in Mission Viejo. And while people accuse the Council of nefarious things,
she and her colleagues are doing the best they can to abide by the law and protect the City and the
citizens they represent. Council Member Bucknum outlined her attendance at the grand opening
of the Potocki Center for the Arts and she encouraged residents to get involved and take advantage
of the amazing classes that will be offered there. She also attended the Polar Bear Plunge at Sierra
Recreation Center and she and Mayor Pro Tem Raths toured the Marguerite Aquatics Center which
will be re-opening in April. She said the Nadadores will be volunteering at the facility this weekend
to help plant the plants that will grace the complex. Council Member Bucknum attended “A Place
for Every Family Play Date” at Pavion Park on the January 14 and she thanked the organizers of
that event. In closing, Council Member Bucknum announced that there are a lot of business ribbon
cuttings on the horizon and it is going to be a great year.

Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell thanked Council Member Bucknum for talking about the district maps
and he echoed what she said. He noted that the Council has an obligation to listen to the public's
input and not put undue influence on the residents. He said the Council Members have been
purposefully listening and not announcing that the outcome should go this way or that way. The
next public hearing will be held on February 13, 2018, and the Council will have to decide what
to do with all the information that has been received and determine what is best for the City.
Council Member Goodell said it was great to see all the Sheriff’s Department Explorers and Police
and Fire first responders attend the meeting for the Employee of the Year awards. He also
appreciated the Nadadores presence in the audience to honor Coach Rose who has an incredible
legacy in Mission Viejo. He said that Bill Rose has been an extraordinary mentor to many people,
not only swimmers, but to families and individuals from all over the country and the world. Council
Member Goodell said that he’s excited to see the aquatics facility when it opens on April 7 and he
hopes residents will turn out for the dedication ceremony, tours of the facility, and a meet and greet
with Olympians.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley announced that she was pleased to represent the City with Council
Member Goodell at the ribbon cutting ceremony for the San Diego County Credit Union. She
encouraged anyone who has a need in that realm to take a look at the services they are offering.
She also attended the Polar Bear Plunge and the grand opening of the Potocki Center for the Arts.
Council Member Kelley thanked staff and the volunteers who made both events very successful.
She noted that she has been attending the monthly Drug Prevention Coalition meetings and
recently, the focus topic was on recreational marijuana. A speaker from the Orange County
Healthcare Agency shared that of the 34 cities in Orange County, the City of Santa Ana is the only
City Council Minutes  8  January 23, 2018
 one that has dispensaries. She said that people may wonder why a City would allow marijuana
sales but she learned that Santa Ana charges a 20% tax so there is money to be made. Council
Member Kelley shared that parents from the Drug Prevention Coalition say, in every case, that the
child they lost to drug abuse began with marijuana. She stated that she is very troubled by the
direction the state is taking and she cautioned parents to keep a close eye on their teens and young
people. In closing, Council Member Kelley announced that the Community of Character word for
the month of January is perseverance.

Mayor Pro Tem Raths

Mayor Pro Tem Raths discussed his attendance at the recent Chamber of Commerce mixer. He
noted that there are a lot of new members coming to the meetings and the Chamber is starting to
be a real force within the City. He announced that the Chamber networking group, Daybreakers,
meets every Tuesday morning from 8:00 to 9:30 a.m. at High Park Tap House and it is great to see
the Chamber moving forward. Mayor Pro Tem Raths also thanked the City for backing the
Chamber with staff help and with financial assistance. He further announced that the Rotary will
host a Texas Hold 'Em fundraiser on April 14 to raise funds for local charities. Of a $65 buy-in,
$50 will go to a charity in the local area and he encouraged local 501cs organizations to register at
http://mvtexasholdem.com.

Mayor Sachs

Mayor Sachs outlined some of his recent interactions including a meeting with the leadership of
the Mission Viejo Chamber of Commerce which is taking new steps towards enhancing the
organization. He also met with the new Chief of Police Services who is getting up to speed and
making a lot of progress with communications, as the City requested. Mayor Sachs said he was
pleased to see both the Orange County Sheriff’s Department (OCSD) and Orange County Fire
Authority (OCFA) Employees of the Year honored this evening and he announced that the OCFA
Best and Bravest Awards Dinner will be held on Friday, February 23, 2018. He discussed the
Orange County firefighters and paramedics who continue to excel including those from Station 9
in Mission Viejo. They train on specific incidents but they cannot train on the unexpected which
was demonstrated when the firefighters were called to help with Hurricane Harvey relief efforts.
There they discovered that the only way to communicate was with their personal cell phones and
the men quickly figured out how to manage that. Mayor Sachs proudly noted that those Mission
Viejo firefighters were credited with over 4,000 rescues within their first two days in Houston.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 8:21 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Sachs adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, February 13, 2018, at 5:00 p.m.

_____________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of February 13, 2018

City Council Minutes  9  January 23, 2018
